Introduction

Flutcom Docs

The complete guide to building zero-dependency, lightning-fast static SPAs.

Why Flutcom?

Flutcom is a lightweight Vanilla JS framework that runs entirely in the browser. It gives you the power of a modern SPA (routing, components, state management) without the massive overhead of Node.js, Webpack, or a Virtual DOM.

We designed Flutcom to bring back the simplicity of the early web, but with the modern developer experience you expect today. You just write HTML, CSS, and JS — and the framework handles the heavy lifting, delivering instant page transitions and native performance.

What can you build with Flutcom?

High-Performance Landing Pages

Create stunning, animated landing pages with zero load time between sections thanks to our built-in hash router.

Interactive Dashboards

Manage complex data using the Global Store. Build admin panels without needing a heavy bundler pipeline.

Dynamic Portfolios

Showcase your work dynamically using reusable components and native HTML imports, keeping your code clean and modular.

Rapid Prototyping

Test ideas in seconds. Just open index.html in your browser and start building instantly, no npm install required.

Requirements

Before installing Flutcom, ensure you have the following prerequisites installed on your system:

  • Node.js 18.0+ (Required only for the CLI and Dev Server)
  • NPM, Yarn or pnpm

To check if you already have them installed, you can run the following commands in your terminal:

Terminal 
# Check Node.js version
node -v

# Check NPM version
npm -v

Don't have Node.js? You can download it directly from nodejs.org.

Installation

For the best development experience, we recommend using NPM to run a local development server with hot-reloading features.

Terminal 
# 1. Create a new project via CLI
npm create flutcom@latest

# 2. Navigate to your project folder
cd my-project

# 3. Start the dev server
npm run dev

There is no compilation step. You can simply serve the source folder directly using any static web server.

Terminal 
# 1. Clone the repository
git clone https://github.com/Mrblour/Flutcom my-project

# 2. Navigate to directory
cd my-project

# 3. Serve using npx or any other server
npx serve . 

# Alternatively, just open index.html directly in your browser!

Quick Start

Let's create your first view in Flutcom to get you familiar with the workflow.

1. resources/views/public/hello.html 
<div class="container py-20 text-center">
  <h1 class="text-4xl text-white font-bold">Hello Flutcom!</h1>
</div>
2. flutcom.config.js 
// Register the route
const config = {
  routes: {
    '#hello': { view: 'resources/views/public/hello.html' }
  }
};

Now navigate to http://localhost:3000/#hello to see your view instantly loaded without restarting the server.

Directory Structure

flutcom/ (Do not touch: core engine)
plugins/ (Your custom global scripts)
resources/
components/ (Reusable UI snippets)
partials/ (Header/Footer)
views/ (Your actual pages)
flutcom.config.js (Main configuration)
index.html (The main shell)

Configuration

The flutcom.config.js file is the heart of your project. It defines your metadata, routes, and global resources.

site

Defines SEO metadata, app name, and the defaultView (what loads when a user visits #/).

partials

Points to your Header and Footer HTML files. Flutcom injects them automatically around your views.

routes

A dictionary mapping URL hashes (like #about) to physical HTML files in your workspace.

resources

An array of global JavaScript plugins that the engine will load and cache automatically.

Routing & Guards

All routes are registered in flutcom.config.js. Navigation happens via hash (#home). You can also protect routes using Guards.

// In flutcom/main.js
const app = new Flutcom({ ... });

// Create a guard to protect the dashboard
app.guard('dashboard', () => {
  const token = localStorage.getItem('auth_token');
  return !!token; // If false, redirects to default route
}, 'login');

Creating Views

Views are the core pages of your application. They are simple HTML fragments stored in the resources/views/ directory.

Rules for Views:

  • Do NOT include <html>, <head>, or <body> tags. The engine injects them directly into the existing index.html shell.
  • Start directly with your layout tags, like <main> or <div>.
  • You can include inline <script> tags. Flutcom safely evaluates them every time the view loads.
resources/views/public/about.html
<!-- Just pure, raw HTML content -->
<main class="container pt-20">
  <h1>About Us</h1>
  <p>We build fast static sites.</p>
</main>

<script>
  console.log("The about view has loaded dynamically!");
</script>

Components (fc-props)

Stop copying and pasting HTML. Flutcom's component system works in two simple steps: create a template once, and inject it anywhere with JSON data.

1. The Component (The Template)

Create a file once. Use {{ variable }} for dynamic text.

resources/components/badge.html
<span class="inline-flex rounded-full border {{ classes }}">
  <i class="{{ icon }}"></i> {{ text }}
</span>

2. The View (Where you use it)

Add an empty container. Tell Flutcom which component to load and pass the JSON data.

resources/views/public/components.html
<!-- Flutcom auto-injects the HTML here! -->
<div 
  fc-component="resources/components/badge.html" 
  fc-props='{"classes": "text-sky-400 border-sky-900", "icon": "bi-info-circle", "text": "Info"}'>
</div>
The Magic

If you ever need to change the design of your badges, you only edit badge.html once. The changes automatically reflect everywhere you used it across your entire website.

Global Store

Built-in reactive state manager. Update the store, and all subscribed UI elements update instantly.

const store = window.flutcomApp.store;

// 1. Subscribe UI element to changes
store.subscribe((key, val) => {
  if(key === 'cart_total') {
    document.getElementById('badge').textContent = val;
  }
});

// 2. Update value anywhere in your app
store.set('cart_total', 5);

Styling & CSS

Flutcom does not enforce any CSS methodology, but it pairs perfectly with Tailwind CSS via CDN. Keep your core styles in the index.html shell to prevent layout shifts.

<!-- Inside index.html <head> -->
<script src="https://cdn.tailwindcss.com"></script>
<link rel="stylesheet" href="assets/css/flutcom.css">

Built-in Modals

The framework ships with a native modal manager plugin. Modals are physical HTML files stored in resources/modals/.

Triggering a modal
<button onclick="window.flutcomModals.open('modal-deploy')">
  Open Deploy
</button>
Closing a modal
<!-- Add this attribute to any button -->
<button data-modal-close>
  Close
</button>

Plugins API

Register global scripts in flutcom.config.js under the resources array. They run once on boot.

// plugins/my-plugin.js
window.myPlugin = {
  sayHello: () => alert("Flutcom is awesome!")
};

Flutcom comes with Modals built-in. Use window.flutcomModals.open('modal-id') to trigger them easily.

Deployment

Since Flutcom has no build step and runs entirely in the browser, deployment is as simple as hosting static files.

GitHub Pages

Just push your code to the main branch and enable Pages. No actions required.

Vercel

Import your repository. Leave the Build Command and Output Directory completely empty.

Traditional Hosting

Upload the folder via FTP to your Apache or Nginx server. It works immediately.
